content.title: What are StringBuilder and StringBuffer?
content.description: StringBuilder and StringBuffer are mutable classes in Java used to modify strings efficiently without creating new objects. StringBuilder is faster, while StringBuffer is thread-safe.

content.content: Unlike the String class, which is immutable, StringBuilder and StringBuffer allow modifications to the same object. They are ideal when performing frequent string operations such as appending, inserting, deleting, or reversing text.

content.title: Why Use StringBuilder or StringBuffer?
content.content: Repeated string modifications using String create many temporary objects. StringBuilder and StringBuffer improve performance by modifying the same object.
StringBuilder is designed for fast string manipulation in single-threaded applications.

content.title: StringBuilder Example
Key Feature
content.description: StringBuilder modifies the existing object instead of creating new String objects, making it much faster for repeated updates.

content.content: StringBuffer works similarly to StringBuilder but synchronizes its methods, making it safe for use by multiple threads.

content.title: StringBuffer Example
Thread Safety
content.content: StringBuffer is synchronized, making it thread-safe, whereas StringBuilder is not synchronized and offers better performance.
Both StringBuilder and StringBuffer provide several methods for efficiently manipulating text.

content.title: StringBuilder Operations

content.content: Both StringBuilder and StringBuffer maintain an internal capacity. When the current capacity is exceeded, Java automatically increases it to accommodate additional characters.

content.title: Capacity Example

items.question: When should StringBuilder be used?
items.answer: When performing many string modifications in single-threaded programs.

items.question: When should StringBuffer be used?
items.answer: When multiple threads access and modify the same string object.

items.question: Why not always use String?
items.answer: Repeated String modifications create many unnecessary objects and reduce performance.

items.question: Where are they commonly used?
items.answer: Text editors, log generation, report creation, and dynamic string processing.

content.title: Notebook vs Printed Book
content.content: A String is like a printed book—you cannot directly modify its pages. StringBuilder and StringBuffer are like notebooks where you can easily erase, insert, and rewrite content without creating a new notebook.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers frequently ask about String vs StringBuilder vs StringBuffer, mutability, synchronization, performance differences, and common string manipulation methods.

items.question: Does append() create a new object?
items.answer: No. It modifies the existing StringBuilder or StringBuffer object.

items.question: Should StringBuffer always be preferred?
items.answer: No. Use StringBuilder unless thread safety is required.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use String for fixed text, StringBuilder for fast mutable strings in single-threaded applications, and StringBuffer when thread safety is required.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: StringBuilder and StringBuffer are mutable classes.
Both modify the same object instead of creating new ones.
StringBuilder is faster because it is not synchronized.
Common methods include append(), insert(), delete(), replace(), and reverse().
